long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Rome to Apulian parents, Melpignano first entered hospitality by helping his mother convert the family's Masseria San Domenico into a hotel. He studied at London's Cass Business School and earned an MBA from Wharton, then worked in investment banking and hotel development. His international experience included corporate planning, investor relations and expansion work for Morgans Hotel Group.

Melpignano returned to Europe in 2007 and took charge of Borgo Egnazia, shaping a new resort around regional architecture, service and local culture. The project became the platform for a wider operating model. In 2023 he founded Egnazia Ospitalità Italiana to manage and advise hotels beyond the family-owned properties. He remains the group's founder and chief executive, while also serving as Altagamma's vice president for hospitality.
